children: Canadian PM Mark Carney has pushed trade diversification as a means to rebuild an economy dealing with a protectionist Trump administration. Trade data indicate that is underway in a notable way. Merchandise-trade figures for July show the level of non-US exports hit a record high of C$25.6 billion--or a 56% increase from January of last year, when President Trump began his second term. During the same period, the value of U.S.-bound exports dropped 11.5%, to C$50.5 billion. Historically, about three-quarters of Canadian exports are U.S. bound. In July, that share stood at 66.4%. (Paul.Vieira@wsj.com, @paulvieira)
